page.title: Tailwind CSS - Rapidly build modern websites without ever leaving your HTML.

findings.title: h3 headings render at 2 different sizes
findings.evidence: “Redefining real-time performance” is 36px while “Browse properties” is 16px (2.25×). Sizes seen: 16px ×1, 36px ×1. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h3 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Card is far taller than its content
findings.evidence: div.isolate.flex is 500×530px but its content occupies 11% of that; 392px of empty space sits under the last line. Nothing inside it needs the height, so a fixed height or min-height is probably set.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height / min-height and let the card size to its content, or fill the space with something that earns it.
findings.citation: Lin 2004: whitespace helps comprehension when it frames content; dead space inside a container just reads as unfinished

findings.title: Head is missing: title is 76 chars (cuts off ~60), canonical
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: AI color palette
findings.fix: Purple/violet gradients and cyan-on-dark are the most recognizable tells of AI-generated UIs. A gradient in one of those hues is the tell on its own; flat neon ink on a dark ground is charged once a second tell hue joins it. Choose a distinctive, intentional palette.

findings.title: 10 cards nested inside other cards
findings.evidence: 9 outer containers with bordered/shadowed children, e.g. div.relative.flex inside div.relative.border-(--pattern-fg). Every layer of box is a layer the reader has to look through.
findings.fix: Remove the inner border/background and separate items with spacing or a divider. One container per idea.
findings.citation: UXly nested-panel (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #5; Reinecke 2013: visual complexity is the strongest negative predictor of appeal

findings.title: 37 rounded panels on one page
findings.evidence: Rounded corners on every container is one of the ranked vibe-coded tells (#5 in the Reddit corpus).
findings.fix: Round the things that are interactive or elevated; let sections and layout containers stay square.

findings.title: 4 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “Sponsors” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (12)
findings.evidence: div.h-112.p-4 is a radial-gradient wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: 2 marketing buzzwords
findings.evidence: “…WHY TAILWIND CSS? Built for the modern web. text-base te…” · “…e performance Our next-generation rendering engine…”
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'

findings.title: Em-dash overuse
findings.fix: Em-dash saturation in body copy is an AI cadence tell. Advisory only: humans use em-dashes legitimately, so this fires only on saturation — at least 8 em-dashes (— or --) at a density near one per 500 characters of body text — never on a long article that uses a few. Prefer commas, colons, periods, or parentheses.
